editorial.marketOverview: Nasdaq enters November 16–18 with Friday's confirmed technology weakness still the latest cash-session evidence: Nasdaq -0.91%, QQQ -1.19%, SOX -3.4%. The roughly +8.1% SOX weekly rebound is an important counterweight, not evidence that Friday's chip selloff reversed. Weekend closure leaves the bearish elevated-downside assessment unchanged.
editorial.whatChanged: At the November 14 21:34 EST review, there is no new regular-session market response and no newly verified major catalyst. The curated Open Watch file still contains 163 events and was last updated November 13 23:46 UTC. Reuters' export-policy reporting and the published Nvidia earnings calendar remain relevant but were already part of the prior risk picture. No material change is established.
editorial.marketInterpretation: Semiconductor underperformance on Friday is the clearest bearish relative-strength signal; weekly chip strength and equal-weight S&P resilience argue against treating the move as indiscriminate liquidation. Reported ten-year and two-year yields imply +28.3bp only after correct percentage-to-basis-point conversion, and cannot be treated as a synchronized official close. Oil quotes and secondary Fed probabilities are contextual, while absent synchronized volatility and breadth readings limit conviction.
editorial.threeDayPath: Monday November 16: Empire State manufacturing at 08:30 ET and positioning before the event cluster. Tuesday November 17: retail sales 08:30 ET, industrial production 09:15 ET, Nvidia earnings after the close. Wednesday November 18: housing starts 08:30 ET, the first US cash-session response to Nvidia earnings, and FOMC minutes at 14:00 ET. Each directional path depends on realized surprises and trading confirmation, not assumed catalyst outcomes.
editorial.bullCase: Stronger-than-feared Nvidia results and guidance, renewed SOX leadership, broader advancing participation, easing long yields and subdued volatility would support a recovery and invalidate elevated downside risk. The weekly SOX gain demonstrates rebound capacity but is not sufficient confirmation by itself.
editorial.bearCase: A fresh SOX-led decline, rising long yields, broadening weakness or a disappointing Nvidia outlook could intensify selling. Hawkish FOMC-minute interpretation and chip-export uncertainty could amplify pressure, but no new restriction or weekend US market reaction has been verified.
